reason: The Linux OOM killer terminated the Neuron compiler backend during graph compilation. Kernel log: 'Out of memory: Killed process 45043 (walrus_driver) total-vm:80789336kB, anon-rss:48591568kB' under cpuset=np-lastwindow.service.
attempt_history: attempt 1, original instance i-00e7b6117eac3a122: host RAM OOM during compile -- a genuine result, but it also took the suite down and the instance was replaced
attempt 2, this instance: stale-compile-lock deadlock caused by operator kills -- NOT a result, receipt marked as such
attempt 3, this instance with a 64 GiB swapfile present: host RAM OOM during compile again, cleanly reproduced
conclusion: Two independent, genuine host-memory OOMs during compilation on a 124 GiB machine. Sequence length 16384 could not be COMPILED for Trainium2 on trn2.3xlarge. This is a HOST-side toolchain limit, not a statement about whether the graph would fit in the chip's 96 GiB HBM -- compilation never completed, so no HBM figure was ever produced.
swap_note: 63 GiB of swap was free and completely unused at the moment of the kill. The kernel chose to OOM-kill rather than swap the compiler's working set, so adding swap did not mitigate this.
receipt_written_by: hand, from journalctl -k and the systemd cgroup attribution -- the OOM killed the whole unit including the shell, so the driver's own failure handler could not run
